independent_reference.source: Baxter, R. J. (1982), Exactly Solved Models in Statistical Mechanics, Academic Press, section 7.10 (spontaneous magnetization of the square-lattice Ising model). The Yang closed form m(T) = (1 - sinh^-4(2 beta J))^(1/8) at T = 1.0, J = 1 gives m = 0.99927575...; cite-by-edition.

Newman, M. E. J. & Barkema, G. T. (1999), Monte Carlo Methods in Statistical Physics, Oxford University Press, Fig. 3.1 (magnetization curve of the 2D Ising model). The Yang closed form at T = 1.5, J = 1 gives m = 0.98649960...; cite-by-edition (digitized-curve consistency check).

Yang, C. N. (1952), The spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional Ising model, Phys. Rev. 85, 808, Eq. (96): m(T) = (1 - sinh^-4(2 beta J))^(1/8) for T < T_c. At T = 2.0, J = 1, beta = 0.5: sinh(1.0) = 1.1752011936..., m = 0.911319377877496.
